  <title>Geology_Radon_Risk</title>
  <abstract>This dataset shows the uraniferous geology of Washington State at a scale of 1:100,000. It is based on the 1:250,000 scale uraniferous geology dataset that was produced by Washington State Department of Natural Resources (DNR) in 1992, and the more detailed statewide geological mapping (at a scale of 1:100,000) presently available. Both the 1992 and current datasets were made to support studies of radon hazards by the Washington State Department of Health. Radon is a decay product of uranium, and consequently the uranium concentration of underlying rocks and soil is an important determinant of the potential for radon in homes. In this dataset the potential for uranium in the rocks and soil is classified as high, variable, or low.

This map was created to show potential radon levels in the State of Washington for the Washington State Department of Health. It's intended for a rudimentary study of radon hazards, and shouldn't be used at scales larger than 1:100,000.</abstract>
